 Order

This writ petition is filed seeking for following reliefs:
(i) Issue a writ of certiorari or any other appropriate writ, order quashing Preliminary Notification dated 03.11.2006 (Annexure-E) and Final Notification dated 07.05.2007 (Annexure-G) issued by 1st respondent as same are illegal and contrary to provisions of Karnataka Industrial NC: 2023:KHC:39596 Areas Development Board Act and also in violation of principles of natural;
(ii) Issue a writ of mandamus or any other appropriate writ, order or direction,
directing respondents to delete land bearing Sy.no.74/302 measuring 4 acres situated at Bandikodigehalli village, Jala Hobli, Bengaluru North Taluk, Bengaluru District from acquisition and restore lands in favour of petitioner consequent upon quashing Smt. Mary John vs State Of Karnataka on 7 November, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/103620627/
2 Notifications at Annexures-E and G.

sentences.text: 2. Sri Nanja Reddy P.N., learned counsel for petitioner submitted that petitioner was absolute owner of land bearing Sy.no.74/302 of Bandikodigehalli village, Yelahanka Taluk, to an extent of 04 acres as held by Special Deputy Commissioner in order dated 07.09.2016 at Annexure-C.
However, land acquisition proceedings initiated by respondents no.1 and 2 was without notice to petitioner, no award was passed and no compensation was paid.
Therefore, same was being challenged.
3. It was submitted that order at Annexure-C passed in pursuance of direction issued in W.P.no.15030/2009 filed earlier by petitioner would enure to her.
It was submitted that since petitioner had not questioned acquisition proceedings in earlier writ petition, she was entitled to do so herein.

4. On other hand, Sri P.V.Chandrashekar, learned counsel for respondent no.3 referring to its statement of NC: 2023:KHC:39596 objections would submit that after dismissal of earlier writ petition, petitioner had filed W.A.no.697/2014, which came to be dismissed reserving liberty to take such recourse as may be available.
In view of dismissal of writ petition and writ appeal, petitioner cannot now turn around and seek to challenge acquisition proceedings.

5. Relying upon decision of Division Bench of this Court in V.T.Krishnamoorthy vs. State of Karnataka1, it was submitted that since petitioner had expressed interest in earlier writ petition in claiming compensation, she was estopped from questioning acquisition proceedings in present writ petition and thus, sought for dismissal of writ petition.
6. Learned AGA also sought to oppose writ petition.

7. Heard learned counsel and perused writ petition records.
8.

From above, it is seen that petitioner was staking interest in land bearing Sy.no.74/302 to extent of 04 acres of Bandikodigehalli village, which was admittedly acquired by respondents no.1 and 2 for formation of industrial area by ILR 1991 KAR 1183 NC: 2023:KHC:39596 respondent no.3.

Though acquisition was without notice to petitioner, perhaps due to dispute about her interest in acquired land, in W.P.no.15030/2009, petitioner had only sought direction to respondents to pass award in her name.
Said writ petition was disposed of reserving liberty to petitioner to establish his title before Competent authority.

9. After petition was allowed, petitioner filed W.P.no.8280/2013 seeking for direction to respondent authorities to frame award as contemplated under Section 29(3) of Karnataka Industrial Areas Development Act, in favour of petitioner.

Said writ petition was disposed of as per order at Annexure-D with following observations:
"The civil court would hardly be in a position to find the title of the petitioner in view of the above observations.

The petitioner is thus left with little alternative, but to establish her title by recourse to independent proceedings against the State and Smt. Mary John vs State Of Karnataka on 7 November, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/103620627/
3 others, if the law so permits.

entities.text: Smt. Mary John vs State Of Karnataka
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The learned counsel for the petitioner, however, has placed reliance on several authorities to insist that the petitioner shall not driven to file an independent suit and the question of her title could be resolved in the reference.

In the instant case, not only was the award made is the subject matter of criminal proceedings, the grant under which the petitioner claimed, having been held to be bogus, it is presumptuous on the part of the petitioner that a second award should now be made favouring the petitioner and for the State to thereafter seek a reference under section 30 to the civil court.

The same is impermissible as laid down in the above decision."
NC: 2023:KHC:39596 10.
Against said order, petitioner filed W.A.no.697/2014.
While dismissing said appeal under order at Annexure-R1 on 19.08.2021, Division Bench had reserved liberty to avail such recourse as available in law.
11. Sum total of above orders would be that after establishing her title before Civil Court, petitioner could lay claim for compensation.
Said observation would not under in any circumstances, entitle petitioner to question acquisition proceedings, especially, at this length of time.

12. As rightly submitted by Sri P.V.Chandrashekar, learned counsel for respondent no.3, a person,
who elects for compensation, would not entitle to question acquisition.
In that view of matter, I do not find any merits in writ petition.
Hence, writ petition stands dismissed.

Sd/-
